sites.text: description: Consult a stronger model for objective, consultant-style feedback on the session's scope and direction — a second brain for the seat, not a code reviewer. Use when the seat is a lower-tier model (Opus/Sonnet) facing a scope, architecture, or direction call, or when the user asks for "fable's take" / "codex's take" / "get an advisor read". Methods: fable (Fable 5.1, the wise-owl judgment seat — Cris's default for advice; costs extra usage, which he accepts here) | astra (GPT-6 Astra high — cross-vendor judgment, when Cris names it or the seat is Fable) | both (dual blind advisory, Fable + Astra in parallel). Returns a scope verdict, advisory deltas, and ONLY questions that are genuinely undecidable from the repo and conversation.
- The seat is Opus/Sonnet and about to commit to a non-trivial direction (scope, architecture, cut lines, sequencing).
- The user asks for it: "what would fable say about this scope?", "get codex's take", "/advisor".
- When the seat IS Fable 5.1: the fable method is pointless (same brain advising itself). Use **astra** for a cross-vendor second opinion instead.
Resolution order: **spoken choice → `~/.claude/advisor-config.json` → built-in default (fable)**. Judgment-tier models are canonical in the model lanes in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

Temperament rule (Cris, 2026-07-10): **advice is owl work.** Fable 5.1 is the wise owl — the smartest judgment seat — so it is Cris's advisor default despite the extra usage; that cost is accepted HERE specifically. GPT-6 Astra high shares the judgment tier — same tier as Fable until evidence separates them. Legacy Sol, when named, advises at **XHIGH** (advice deserves its top reasoning; the execution lanes are the ones that run high).
| `fable` | Fable 5.1 | headless CLI (Step 2), `--effort high` (raise only on explicit ask) | **Cris's default for advice.** The owl: scope verdicts, direction, what-to-cut judgment. |

| `astra` | GPT-6 Astra at **high** (model from config) | `codex exec` read-only | When Cris names it ("advisory astra"), when the seat IS Fable (cross-vendor second opinion), or when the advice should ride the ChatGPT pool. |
| `both` | Fable 5.1 + Astra high, blind, in parallel | both invocations in Step 2 | When Cris says "both". See Dual advisory below. |
| `sol` | GPT-5.6 Sol at **xhigh** (legacy) | `codex exec -m gpt-5.6-sol` read-only | Only when Cris names it. |

First-time users (no config file exists): ask once via AskUserQuestion (codex — needs `npm i -g @openai/codex` + auth | fable | claude opus), then save the choice to `~/.claude/advisor-config.json`. Copy `advisor-config.example.json` from this skill's folder as the starting point. A spoken one-run choice never changes the saved default.

"Advisory both" runs **fable and astra blind, in parallel** on the same brief — no rebuttal rounds, no negotiated compromise. The seat then resolves factual disagreements itself against the repo, and presents judgment disagreements to Cris steelmanned, both sides — it never picks the winner. (Canonical protocol: the model-lanes table in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.)
**astra** (brief lives at an absolute path; verdict on stdout, logs on stderr):
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=high \

**fable** — headless CLI, **NEVER the Agent tool**: Agent-tool `model: fable` spawns silently downgrade to sonnet in some harnesses (verified via session logs, 2026-07-11). The CLI is the proven path — same mechanism as `/code-review fable` and the Atlas fable lane:
--model claude-fable-5-1 --effort high --output-format json \

Parse the JSON envelope: the advisory text is `.result`, and the `modelUsage` keys **must include `claude-fable-5-1`**. If they don't, the call ran on the wrong model — abort, tell the user, and never present another model's output as fable. Check `.is_error` is false before trusting `.result`, and never branch on `$?` — piping the output masks a failed call as exit 0.
{ "method": "fable", "codexModel": "gpt-6-astra", "codexEffort": "high" }
Precedence: spoken choice for one run → this file → built-in default (fable). Changing the codex model (at a new model's release) is one edit here; nothing in the skill hardcodes it.
- **The advisor never edits.** Read-only sandbox for codex; no Edit/Write for the fable agent.
- **Prove the model.** Every fable call verifies the envelope's `modelUsage` contains `claude-fable-5-1`. A silent downgrade is a failed call, not an answer — report it, don't relabel it.
- **Fable is deliberate, never default.** It costs extra usage; auto-selecting it silently is a bug in the seat's judgment.
"method": "fable",
"codexModel": "gpt-6-astra",
"codexEffort": "high"
model: "sonnet",

description: Build something through the Frame -> Bar -> Judge loop. Runs four phases (Understand, Shape, Build, Judge) — the session model orchestrates and advises, implementer subagents type per the model-lanes doctrine (guided phases, callbacks on demand), GPT-6 Astra high independently attacks the plan (Bounce) and grades the result (Grade), and the human judges. Pick the implementer with "/build astra|sol|grok|opus|sonnet" (or plain English); unspecified means the orchestrator routes by the lanes doctrine. Use for any real build where you want it done right and self-correcting. Scales down: a lightweight mode handles small single-outcome work (one implementer call, no plan/Bounce/Grade scaffold) so small-but-real tasks route here too — only true two-minute edits stay out.

**The session model orchestrates and guides. A cheaper implementer types. A different brain verifies. The human judges.** (Doctrine v3, 2026-07-08.) Roles follow the seat: whatever model is running this session (Fable 5.1 when Cris set it, Opus 5 otherwise) is the orchestrator, and it does NOT type the bulk of the code. Pick the implementer lane per the **model-lanes doctrine** in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (GPT-6 Astra medium default, GPT-5.6 Sol medium legacy backup, Opus for taste-heavy work, Sonnet only as an Opus orchestrator's subagent). Whoever implements never grades their own work.
| Understand (explore) | orchestrator + Explore subagents (sonnet) | conclusions only come back; bulk file dumps stay out of the orchestrator's context |
| Shape: **Bounce** (attack the plan) | GPT-6 Astra high | `codex exec` (read-only) |

| Build (guided steps) | implementer — **GPT-6 Astra medium default, GPT-5.6 Sol medium legacy backup** (via codex CLI), Opus 5 for taste-heavy work (frontend, design, copy); user's spoken lane wins (below) | the guided-step loop below |
| **Grade** (verify build vs bar) | GPT-6 Astra high (flips to a Claude grader — fable — when a GPT lane implemented; see below) | `codex exec` (read-only) |
### Choosing the implementer — `/build astra | sol | grok | opus | sonnet`

Name the lane and it wins for this run: `/build astra`, `/build sol`, or plain English ("build this with opus"). **A named lane is binding for the entire run — every phase, start to finish.** The orchestrator does not re-route mid-build, does not "upgrade" a phase it finds hard, and does not silently fall back. No lane named → the orchestrator routes by the model lanes in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and says which lane it picked and why in one line.

**Unnamed routing** (lanes update, Cris, 2026-09-04): default → **astra** (GPT-6 Astra medium); sustained "keep going until it's done" grinds → **sol** (the legacy workhorse; watch for overbuilding); frontend, UI, design, copy → **opus**; mechanical single-file work → **sonnet**; **grok** only when Cris names it (benched until there's data). Record which lane won or lost — the ranking earns itself.

- **Grader swap (grader is never the author, at the model-family level):** claude-lane implementers (sonnet/opus) → GPT-6 Astra high grades, the default. **GPT implementer (astra/sol) → the Grade flips to a Claude brain** (Fable 5.1 via headless CLI — `claude -p --model claude-fable-5-1 --effort high`, never an Agent-tool spawn, which silently downgrades to sonnet; verify `modelUsage` lists `claude-fable-5-1`) so no family grades its own work. **Grok implementer → GPT-6 Astra high grades** (a third family; either non-grok judgment model is valid).

- Fable is not an implementer lane — the Judgment lane types specs and verdicts, not code (and it burns extra usage). An explicit user demand still wins, as always, but the skill never routes there on its own.

This keeps the expensive model's tokens on judgment (briefs, callback answers, checkpoint reviews — all small) and the volume tokens on the cheap implementer. **Standing escalation — but fix the brief before the builder:** if the implementer misses the bar twice on the same step, first re-read the phase brief; if the spec under-determined the choice, sharpen the brief and re-issue at the same lane (a better brief is cheaper than a bigger model). If the brief was adequate, redo the step on the other default builder (astra ↔ sol); if both miss the same criterion, that is the mis-scope signal — stop and surface it to the driver rather than climbing further. Judge the output, not the price tag. **Without asking when the orchestrator picked the lane; ask first when the user named it** (`/build codex` and friends) — a named lane is the user's decision, so surface the stuck criterion and let them choose to escalate or hold.
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=high \
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=medium \
codex exec resume <thread_id> --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=medium \

`resume` does NOT accept `-s/--sandbox` — it inherits the sandbox policy from the session it resumes, which is why phase 1 must be the one that sets `workspace-write`. It does accept `-m`, `-c`, `-o`, `--json`, `--skip-git-repo-check`. Prefer an explicit `thread_id` over `--last`: the Bounce and Grade gates run in the same cwd, so `--last` can silently resume the wrong session. On the sol lane, swap `-m gpt-5.6-sol` into the build calls (same efforts); the gates stay on the judgment tier regardless of lane.
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=high \

2. **Shape** (orchestrator drafts, GPT-6 Astra attacks). Draft `plan.md`: the outcome, the steps, and a checklist of acceptance criteria where **each criterion is checkable by a command, test, or observable behavior**, plus how each will be verified. Then run the **Bounce** (codex command above), fold its real gaps into the plan, and show the driver the criteria to sharpen and approve (Bar).

3. **Build** (implementer lane — Astra medium default, Sol/Opus per the doctrine or the user's `/build <lane>` choice). Implement against `plan.md`. After each step, run the deterministic checks (`verify.sh` / tests), read pass/fail, fix, repeat. Log decisions to `log.md`. When the deterministic checks pass, run the **Grade** (codex command above) for the independent verdict. If Grade returns any FAIL, fix and re-grade. Loop until Grade is clean or the cap is hit. **QA option:** when acceptance criteria include browser-observable behavior a script can't assert, `/qa-tester` (per `~/.claude/skills/qa-tester/SKILL.md`) is available between Grade and Judge — hand it the target URL, the browser-checkable criteria verbatim, and setup steps. Not mandatory: run it when manual verification would cost the driver real time; skip it when Grade plus the deterministic checks already cover the bar — and state which in the Judge handoff, so a skipped QA run is a visible choice, never a silent one.

Agent lifecycle is published to `~/.cmuxterm/events.jsonl`. **Read state from the event bus, not from the screen.** Both lanes emit regardless of vendor — Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol) and Claude Code both appear as `source`; Claude Code hooks are injected automatically by the cmux Claude wrapper, other agents via `cmux hooks setup`.
cmux hooks setup codex|grok|antigravity|opencode             # specific agent
Native session-resume supported for: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Pi, Amp, Cursor CLI, Gemini, Antigravity, Rovo Dev, Hermes, Copilot, CodeBuddy, Factory, Qoder.

description: Single-pass code review of the current branch's diff. Reviewer tiers picked by how you invoke it — GPT-6 Astra high default (efficient), "fable" for the premium Fable 5.1 judgment pass, "both" for a dual Astra+Fable review, "sol" for the legacy GPT-5.6 Sol pass, "claude" for the opus+sonnet+sonnet team. It reports findings; you confirm which to fix and the agent applies them in-context. No auto-fix, no loop — one review pass, you stay in control.

Review the committed diff for **code correctness** — bugs, regressions, edge cases, error handling, data integrity — judged against what the branch was supposed to do. **One review pass** with GPT-6 Astra high (the default reviewer), then the findings come back to *me* and **you decide what to fix**. I apply the confirmed fixes in-context — fast, no re-spawning a model, no loop.

- Default reviewer = **Codex GPT-6 Astra high** (the judgment-tier default — canonical lanes in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`). `REVIEW_REVIEWER=claude` uses the **Claude multi-agent** reviewer instead (parallel lenses; also for when Codex isn't installed → `npm i -g @openai/codex`). Codex effort default is **high**; `REVIEW_EFFORT=xhigh` raises it for one run.
| `/code-review` (or `codex`) | Codex GPT-6 Astra high — **one agent** | The efficient default. Everyday PRs. Saying "codex" picks it explicitly. |
| `/code-review sol` | GPT-5.6 Sol high (`REVIEW_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol`) — one agent | The legacy reviewer. A second GPT flavor without spending Fable. |

| `/code-review fable` | **Fable 5.1 — ONE agent, one comprehensive pass, never a team** (`REVIEW_REVIEWER=claude REVIEW_CLAUDE_MODEL=claude-fable-5-1`), **effort high by default** (`REVIEW_FABLE_EFFORT=high` or "fable on high" to raise for one run) | The premium judgment pass. Costs extra usage on Max; reserve for changes where being wrong is expensive (payments, order logic, auth, migrations). Single session, same as the Atlas fable lane. |

| `/code-review both` | GPT-6 Astra high **and** Fable 5.1 | Maximum confidence: run the astra pass, then the fable pass, and present ONE merged list — findings both models flagged first (near-certain real), then each model's uniques. |
| `/code-review claude` | Claude multi-agent team (**opus + sonnet + sonnet lenses, all at effort xhigh**) — the ONLY multi-agent tier | Small/routine diffs, or a cheap second flavor. |

**Plain English works too** — "code review this with fable", "review it with both" — the phrase picks the tier for that run via the env overrides. These one-run choices never change the durable default (env var → config file → built-in default precedence).
- Everything else → **gpt-6-astra** (the default).
- Risk paths (payments, money math, auth, migrations, order-correctness, security) or >400 changed lines → **fable**; the very highest stakes → **both**.

For `both`: run the script twice (once with the codex env, once with the fable env — each writes its own `reviews/<ts>/` report), then merge the two findings lists in-context before Step 2. Do not double-fix: one merged list, one confirmation round.
**Codex reasoning default is high** (Cris, 2026-07-10). Raise it for one run by saying so ("review on xhigh") or `REVIEW_EFFORT=xhigh`; the durable default stays high.
- **GPT-6 Astra high (default):** `{ "reviewer": "codex", "model": "gpt-6-astra", "effort": "high" }`
- **GPT-5.6 Sol high (legacy):** `{ "reviewer": "codex", "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "effort": "high" }`

- **Claude team (opus + sonnet + sonnet):** `{ "reviewer": "claude" }` — the default claudeModel (sonnet) runs the mixed team; an explicit different claudeModel (e.g. `claude-fable-5-1`) runs **one comprehensive agent** on that model instead — premium tiers are always a single session, never a team.

"gpt-5.6-sol-high (legacy)": { "reviewer": "codex", "model": "gpt-5.6-sol", "effort": "high" },

description: How to delegate work to another AI agent (Grok, Codex, Claude Code, Hermes) — picking the right agent, sending prompts to TUI agents, polling progress. Read BEFORE any `cmux send`/`tmux send-keys` to an agent, or whenever delegating, relaying, spawning, or orchestrating agent-to-agent work.

**Two lanes type; the rest talk.** GPT-6 Astra medium (default) and GPT-5.6 Sol medium (legacy backup) are the builders. Opus and Sonnet narrate and critique instead of shipping, so a diff is not their deliverable — except frontend, which is Opus's. Grok is benched until there's data. Fable never builds. (Lanes update, Cris, 2026-09-04.)

- **Default build → Codex CLI, GPT-6 Astra medium.** Different strengths (subagents, end-to-end autonomy), still unproven as a builder — record wins and losses so the ranking earns itself. On a ChatGPT Pro plan — effectively unlimited, **don't ration it**; bulk grind spends there instead of the shared Claude Max pool.
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=medium \

- **Sustained "keep going until it's done" grinds → Codex CLI, GPT-5.6 Sol medium (legacy).** The relentless workhorse; watch its diff for overbuilding. Swap `-m gpt-5.6-sol` into the command above. `terra` is the cheaper everyday tier if Cris asks for it.

- **Grok CLI, grok-4.6 high — only when Cris names it** (benched until there's data; capable, ranks above Opus as a builder). **`--always-approve` is required**: with only `--permission-mode acceptEdits` the headless turn announces the edit and returns `stopReason: cancelled` having written nothing.
grok -p "<self-contained brief>" -m grok-4.6 --effort high --always-approve \

- **Reviewing, grading, attacking a plan → Codex CLI, GPT-6 Astra high.** The **default** reviewer across the board: `/build`'s Bounce and Grade gates and `/code-review`'s default tier. Always `--sandbox read-only` — the verifier never edits. **Never route a review to Grok** — it is a build lane only.

- **Frontend / design / copy taste, and anything where a cheap-model miss is expensive → Opus 5 subagent** (Agent tool, `model: opus`). The one build domain Opus keeps, and it is better than Grok there.
- **Mechanical, spec-fully-determined single-file work → Sonnet 5 subagent** (Agent tool, `model: sonnet`). Bottom of the stack; not a lane for anything with a design call in it.

- **Specs, commitment boundaries, premium review verdicts → Fable 5.1**, via headless CLI only (`claude -p --model claude-fable-5-1 --effort high`). Never the Agent tool — `model: fable` silently downgrades to sonnet. Cost-gated: deliberate, never default.

**The grader is never the author, at the model-family level.** Claude implemented → GPT-6 Astra high grades. GPT implemented (Astra/Sol) → a Claude brain (Fable) grades. Grok implemented → either non-grok judgment model grades. Never route both sides of a build to the same vendor.
name: fable-safe-prompt

description: Rewrite a user's prompt to reduce the chance it trips Claude Fable 5's server-side safety classifiers (cyber/bio guardrails that force-route to Opus 5 or return stop_reason "refusal"). Use when the user hands you a prompt that touches cybersecurity, auth, exploits, malware, pentesting, or other dual-use topics and asks to make it "Fable-safe", "guardrail-safe", "won't get flagged/refused/downgraded", or to rewrite it so Fable 5 won't block it.
# Fable-Safe Prompt

Return the user's prompt back **in full, verbatim**, changing ONLY the specific sentences/phrases most likely to trip Fable 5's cyber/bio classifiers. Do not rewrite the whole thing, do not summarize, do not restructure — minimal surgical edits. Keep the actual goal and all benign text exactly as written. This lowers false positives — it does **not** guarantee no trigger.

Fable 5 runs 3 input classifiers: **cyber**, **bio/chem**, **reasoning_extraction**. Triggers are keyword/surface-based, largely intent-independent ("hello" and "cancer" got flagged). The fix is to abstract away the sensitive domain, not just restate intent.
4. If the task is genuinely offensive (pentest, exploit repro, malware analysis): say plainly no edit makes it Fable-safe — use an Opus 5 fallback or vetted Mythos, not Fable 5.

**Hard truth:** you can't reliably stop Fable 5 guardrails. Robust API setups also treat `stop_reason: "refusal"` (HTTP 200, `stop_details.category` = `cyber`/`bio`) as a route to an Opus 5 fallback — mention only if the user controls the integration.

description: Run an evidence-based investigation loop to reach a defensible conclusion (root cause, "is X true?", "which option is actually better", "did this change cause that?"). Forces a proof-bar up front, verifies every claim with a real command or query, runs an adversarial disprove pass in a fresh context, and writes the evidence to files. Investigator method is selectable — codex (GPT-6 Astra high, the default) | claude team | fable — via "/investigate <method>" or plain English ("investigate this with fable"). Use for any question where being right matters and a confident guess would be costly.
| 2. Explore | orchestrator + Explore subagents (sonnet) | conclusions only come back; bulk file/log dumps stay out of the orchestrator's context |

| 4. Verify | fan-out subagents (sonnet default, opus for concurrency/subtle checks) | one subagent per hypothesis, in parallel, each carrying the 5-part contract; returns CONFIRMED, KILLED, or UNVERIFIED plus the pasted evidence, never a raw log dump |
